intro: Now you can talk about the past, so let's tell stories! In this lesson you'll put events in order with **first, then, next, after that** and **finally**, join them with **before, after** and **when**, and show what happened as a result with **so**. Warm-up: what was the first thing you did this morning?
teachingNotes: Stories are told in the past simple (regular -ed and the irregular core list: went, had, got, saw, ate, bought, made, came, took, said, did, drank) plus was/were. In A1 the learner used first / then / after that / finally for daily routines in the simple present; now the same words order past events. Every verb in the story stays in the past: watch for *'After I finish work, I went home' (two times in one sentence).

Order words: First (the first event), then / next / after that (the middle events: they mean almost the same, so encourage mixing them), Finally (the last event, or something that happens after a long wait: We waited for an hour. Finally, the bus came). Commas: usually after First, Next, After that and Finally; usually none after Then. Two traps: 'After' alone at the start is not a replacement for 'After that' (*'After, we went home'), and 'At first' is not 'First': at first = awalnya, before something changed (At first I didn't like the job, but now I like it).

before / after / when + subject + verb join two events in one sentence: After I finished work, I went home. = I went home after I finished work. Comma only when the linker part comes first. The node's common error comes from Indonesian 'Setelah …, lalu …': *'After I finished work, then I went home'. after/before already show the order, so no then in the second part. Also watch for a missing subject (*'After finish work, I went home'; 'Setelah selesai kerja' has no 'saya'): say 'After I finished work' or 'After work'. before/after + a noun is fine too: after lunch, before work. 'After finishing work' is correct English but not taught here: accept it, don't teach it.

when = ketika / saat: the two things happen at the same moment, or one comes right after the other: When I got home, my mother was in the kitchen. When the rain stopped, we went out. Use the past simple or was/were in both parts. Don't teach the past continuous (was walking) or while here.

so (jadi / makanya) introduces the RESULT; because (karena, from a1-conjunctions) introduces the REASON: It rained, so I stayed home. = I stayed home because it rained. The node's common error is the Indonesian 'Karena …, jadi …' pattern: *'Because it rained, so I stayed home'. One sentence takes ONE of them, never both. Second Indonesian trap: 'akhirnya' often means 'so' (Hujan, akhirnya kami di rumah): that's so, not finally. 'so' also means 'very' (so hot = panas sekali): a different job, just mention it if the learner asks. 'It rained. So I stayed home.' is fine in speech; practise the comma pattern for writing.

Limits: past simple, was/were and the simple present only; no past continuous, present perfect, will, going to, although, however, then-as-'in that case', or as a result / therefore. Real contexts: trips to Bandung or Yogyakarta, work in Jakarta, ojek, warung, market, rain. When the learner writes a story, praise the order and correct one thing at a time (usually the verb tense or a double linker).

keyPoints.title: Order words: first, then, next, after that, finally
keyPoints.explanation: To tell a story in order, start the sentences with order words. First = the first event. Then, next and after that = the events in the middle; they mean almost the same, so mix them. Finally = the last event, or the end of a long wait. The verbs stay in the past simple. Usually there's a comma after First, Next, After that and Finally, but not after Then.

examples.en: First, we took the train to Bandung.
examples.id: Pertama-tama, kami naik kereta ke Bandung.

examples.en: Then we had lunch at a warung.
examples.id: Lalu kami makan siang di warung.

examples.en: Finally, we went back to the hotel.

id.title: Kata urutan: first, then, next, after that, finally
id.explanation: Untuk bercerita secara berurutan, awali kalimat dengan kata urutan. First = kejadian pertama. Then, next dan after that = kejadian di tengah; artinya hampir sama, jadi pakai bergantian. Finally = kejadian terakhir, atau akhir dari menunggu lama. Kata kerjanya tetap past simple. Biasanya ada koma setelah First, Next, After that dan Finally, tapi tidak setelah Then.

keyPoints.title: before, after, when + subject + verb
keyPoints.explanation: before (sebelum), after (setelah) and when (ketika / saat) join two events in one sentence. After them, use a subject and a verb: after I finished work (or a noun: after work). You can put this part first (with a comma) or second (no comma). Don't add then: after and before already show the order. Both verbs are in the past.

examples.en: After I finished work, I went home.
I had breakfast before I went to work.
When I arrived at the station, the train was already there.
examples.id: Ketika saya sampai di stasiun, keretanya sudah ada.

id.title: before, after, when + subjek + kata kerja
id.explanation: before (sebelum), after (setelah) dan when (ketika / saat) menggabungkan dua kejadian dalam satu kalimat. Setelahnya, pakai subjek dan kata kerja: after I finished work (atau kata benda: after work). Bagian ini boleh di depan (pakai koma) atau di belakang (tanpa koma). Jangan tambah then: after dan before sudah menunjukkan urutannya. Kedua kata kerjanya past.

keyPoints.title: so for a result (not with because)
keyPoints.explanation: so (jadi / makanya) comes before the result: reason, so result. because comes before the reason. Use one of them, never both in one sentence: It rained, so I stayed home. = I stayed home because it rained. Not 'Because it rained, so I stayed home'. And when Indonesian 'akhirnya' means 'jadi', use so, not finally.

examples.en: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
examples.id: Saya capek, jadi saya tidur lebih awal.

examples.en: I went to bed early because I was tired.
examples.id: Saya tidur lebih awal karena saya capek.

id.title: so untuk akibat (tidak bersama because)
id.explanation: so (jadi / makanya) ada sebelum akibatnya: alasan, so akibat. because ada sebelum alasannya. Pakai salah satu saja, jangan dua-duanya dalam satu kalimat: It rained, so I stayed home. = I stayed home because it rained. Bukan 'Because it rained, so I stayed home'. Dan kalau 'akhirnya' dalam bahasa Indonesia artinya 'jadi', pakai so, bukan finally.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with First or Finally: ___, I turned on my laptop. Then I read my emails.
guidedPractice.hint: It's the first thing in the story.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with before or after: I checked the price ___ I bought the shoes.
guidedPractice.hint: Which came first: checking the price or buying?

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: After I got home, then I had a shower.
expected: after i got home i had a shower
i had a shower after i got home
guidedPractice.hint: after already shows the order. Take out one word.

guidedPractice.prompt: Join the two sentences with so: The bus was full. We took a taxi.
expected: the bus was full so we took a taxi

independentPractice.prompt: What did you do last Saturday? Write three sentences. Start them with First, Then and Finally.
independentPractice.hint: First, I … Then I … Finally, I … (verbs in the past: went, had, watched)

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about yesterday with when: When I got to work, …
independentPractice.hint: Both verbs in the past, and no then.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about a problem you had last week. Use so for the result.
independentPractice.hint: My phone was dead, so I …

assessment.prompt: Complete the story with First, Then and Finally (use each word once). Write the three words in order: ___, I went to the ATM. ___ I bought some fruit at the market. ___, I went home and cooked dinner.
assessment.rubric: Correct: First, Then, Finally (first event, middle event, last event). Finally in the middle or First not first = 30. Two of the three right = 60.

assessment.prompt: Complete with First or Finally: We waited at the bus stop for an hour. ___, the bus came!
assessment.rubric: Correct: Finally (the end of a long wait, = akhirnya). 'First' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with before or after: Rina washed the vegetables ___ she cooked them.
assessment.rubric: Correct: before (she washed them first, then cooked them). 'after' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: After we had lunch, then we went back to the office.
acceptableAnswers: after we had lunch we went back to the office
we went back to the office after we had lunch
after lunch we went back to the office
we went back to the office after lunch
we had lunch and then we went back to the office
assessment.rubric: Correct: After we had lunch, we went back to the office (no then: after already shows the order). Then removed but a verb changed to the present ('After we have lunch') = 50. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Join the two sentences with when: I got home. My mother was in the kitchen.
acceptableAnswers: when i got home my mother was in the kitchen
my mother was in the kitchen when i got home
assessment.rubric: Correct: When I got home, my mother was in the kitchen (or: My mother was in the kitchen when I got home). Extra 'then' = 60. 'When I get home' = 50. when before the wrong part ('When my mother was in the kitchen, I got home') = 30.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: Because the shop was closed, so we went to the warung.
acceptableAnswers: the shop was closed so we went to the warung
because the shop was closed we went to the warung
we went to the warung because the shop was closed
assessment.rubric: Correct: The shop was closed, so we went to the warung. / Because the shop was closed, we went to the warung. (one linker only). because and so swapped ('The shop was closed because we went to the warung') = 0. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Join the two sentences with so: My phone was broken. I bought a new one.
acceptableAnswers: my phone was broken so i bought a new one
my phone was broken so i bought a new phone
assessment.rubric: Correct: My phone was broken, so I bought a new one. 'I bought a new one, so my phone was broken' (result and reason swapped) = 0. 'Because my phone was broken, so I bought …' = 30. With because instead of so ('I bought a new one because my phone was broken') = 60: correct English, but the task asks for so.

blocks.text:
In A1 you used **first, then, after that** and **finally** to tell your normal day: *First, I get up.* Now you can tell a **story** about the past with the same words. The only change: the verbs are in the **past simple** (*went, had, bought, watched*).
- **First** = pertama-tama: the first event
- **Then** = lalu, kemudian
- **Next** = berikutnya, selanjutnya
- **After that** = setelah itu
- **Finally** = terakhir: the last event. It can also mean **akhirnya** after a long wait: *We waited for two hours. Finally, the plane arrived.*

**Then, next** and **after that** mean almost the same thing. Use them in turns, so you don't say *then, then, then*. A comma after *First, Next, After that* and *Finally* is usual; after *Then* we usually don't write one.

id.text:
Di A1 kamu memakai **first, then, after that** dan **finally** untuk menceritakan hari biasamu: *First, I get up.* Sekarang kamu bisa menceritakan **kejadian di masa lalu** dengan kata yang sama. Bedanya cuma satu: kata kerjanya **past simple** (*went, had, bought, watched*).
- **First** = pertama-tama: kejadian pertama
- **Then** = lalu, kemudian
- **Next** = berikutnya, selanjutnya
- **After that** = setelah itu
- **Finally** = terakhir: kejadian terakhir. Bisa juga berarti **akhirnya** setelah menunggu lama: *We waited for two hours. Finally, the plane arrived.*

**Then, next** dan **after that** artinya hampir sama. Pakai bergantian supaya kamu tidak bilang *then, then, then*. Koma setelah *First, Next, After that* dan *Finally* itu biasa; setelah *Then* biasanya tidak pakai koma.

rows.en: Last Sunday, Budi went to Bandung.
rows.id: Minggu lalu, Budi pergi ke Bandung.

rows.en: First, he took the train from Gambir.
rows.id: Pertama-tama, dia naik kereta dari Gambir.

rows.en: Then he had lunch at a warung.
rows.id: Lalu dia makan siang di warung.

rows.en: Next, he visited his aunt.
rows.id: Berikutnya, dia mengunjungi tantenya.

rows.en: After that, he bought some clothes.
rows.id: Setelah itu, dia membeli beberapa baju.

rows.en: Finally, he took the train back to Jakarta.
rows.id: Terakhir, dia naik kereta kembali ke Jakarta.

blocks.text: Two small traps. **After** alone is not the same as **after that**: say *After that, we went home*, not 'After, we went home'. **After** needs something after it: *after that, after lunch, after the film*. And **At first** is not **First**: *at first* means 'awalnya' (and then something changed): *At first I didn't like Jakarta, but now I like it.* For step one of a story, just say **First**.

id.text: Dua jebakan kecil. **After** saja tidak sama dengan **after that**: katakan *After that, we went home*, bukan 'After, we went home'. **After** butuh sesuatu di belakangnya: *after that, after lunch, after the film*. Lalu **At first** bukan **First**: *at first* artinya 'awalnya' (lalu ada yang berubah): *At first I didn't like Jakarta, but now I like it.* Untuk langkah pertama sebuah cerita, cukup pakai **First**.

blocks.prompt: Rina's day yesterday: First, she went to the bank. Then she had coffee with a friend. ___, she went home.
blocks.explain: Going home is the last event of the story, so use **Finally**. First is for the first event, and Before needs something after it (before lunch).

id.prompt: Hari Rina kemarin. Lengkapi: First, she went to the bank. Then she had coffee with a friend. ___, she went home.
id.explain: Pulang ke rumah adalah kejadian terakhir di cerita itu, jadi pakai **Finally**. First untuk kejadian pertama, dan Before butuh sesuatu di belakangnya (before lunch).

blocks.text:
**before** (sebelum), **after** (setelah, sesudah) and **when** (ketika, saat) join **two events in one sentence**. After them you need a **subject + verb** (the subject = who does it: *I, Rina, we*): *after **I finished** work*. Or just a noun: *after work, before lunch*.

The linker part can go **first**, with a comma, or **second**, with no comma. The meaning is the same:
- *After I finished work, I went home.* = *I went home after I finished work.*

**when** means the two things happen at the same moment, or one comes right after the other: *When the class ended, the students went out.* In a story, **both verbs are in the past**.

id.text:
**before** (sebelum), **after** (setelah, sesudah) dan **when** (ketika, saat) menggabungkan **dua kejadian dalam satu kalimat**. Setelah kata ini kamu butuh **subjek + kata kerja** (subjek = siapa yang melakukan: *I, Rina, we*): *after **I finished** work*. Atau cukup kata benda: *after work, before lunch*.

Bagian dengan kata penghubung ini boleh di **depan**, pakai koma, atau di **belakang**, tanpa koma. Artinya sama:
- *After I finished work, I went home.* = *I went home after I finished work.*

**when** artinya dua hal terjadi pada saat yang sama, atau yang satu langsung setelah yang lain: *When the class ended, the students went out.* Dalam cerita, **kedua kata kerjanya past**.

rows.en: Before I went to work, I had breakfast.
rows.id: Sebelum berangkat kerja, saya sarapan.

id.note: bagian dengan kata penghubung di depan → koma

rows.en: I had breakfast before I went to work.
rows.id: Saya sarapan sebelum berangkat kerja.

rows.en: After Rina got her salary, she bought a new bag.
rows.id: Setelah Rina menerima gaji, dia membeli tas baru.

rows.en: When I arrived at the station, the train was already there.
rows.id: Ketika saya sampai di stasiun, keretanya sudah ada.

rows.en: Dimas called his mother after work.
rows.id: Dimas menelepon ibunya sepulang kerja.

blocks.text: Indonesian trap: we often say *Setelah selesai kerja, **lalu** saya pulang.* In English, **after** and **before** already show the order, so there's **no then** in the second part: *After I finished work, I went home*, not 'After I finished work, then I went home'. Two more things from Indonesian: *Setelah selesai kerja* has no *saya*, but English needs the subject (*After **I** finished work*, not 'After finish work'). And keep **both** verbs in the past: not 'After I finish work, I went home'.

id.text: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kita sering bilang *Setelah selesai kerja, **lalu** saya pulang.* Dalam bahasa Inggris, **after** dan **before** sudah menunjukkan urutannya, jadi **tidak ada then** di bagian kedua: *After I finished work, I went home*, bukan 'After I finished work, then I went home'. Dua hal lagi dari bahasa Indonesia: *Setelah selesai kerja* tidak memakai *saya*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh subjeknya (*After **I** finished work*, bukan 'After finish work'). Dan pakai past untuk **kedua** kata kerjanya: bukan 'After I finish work, I went home'.

blocks.prompt: We waited at home all morning. ___ the rain stopped, we went out.
blocks.explain: They went out at the moment the rain stopped, so use **When**. Before is wrong: they waited, so they didn't go out in the rain. So can't start this sentence: it goes before a result.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: We waited at home all morning. ___ the rain stopped, we went out.
id.explain: Mereka keluar saat hujannya berhenti, jadi pakai **When**. Before salah: mereka menunggu, jadi mereka tidak keluar waktu masih hujan. So tidak bisa dipakai di sini: so diletakkan sebelum akibat.

material.title: so for the result, because for the reason

blocks.text:
You know **because** (karena): it comes before the **reason**. Now meet **so** (jadi, makanya): it comes before the **result**, what happened next because of it. The order is: **reason, so result**. Put a comma before so.
- *It rained, **so** I stayed home.* (reason: it rained → result: I stayed home)
- *I stayed home **because** it rained.* (the same story the other way round)

One sentence takes **so** or **because**, never both. In Indonesian we often say *Karena hujan, **jadi** saya di rumah*. Translated word by word, that's 'Because it rained, so I stayed home', which is wrong in English.

id.text:
Kamu sudah kenal **because** (karena): kata ini ada sebelum **alasan**. Sekarang kenalan dengan **so** (jadi, makanya): kata ini ada sebelum **akibat**, yaitu apa yang terjadi karena hal itu. Urutannya: **alasan, so akibat**. Pakai koma sebelum so.
- *It rained, **so** I stayed home.* (alasan: hujan → akibat: saya di rumah)
- *I stayed home **because** it rained.* (cerita yang sama, urutannya dibalik)

Satu kalimat memakai **so** atau **because**, jangan dua-duanya. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering bilang *Karena hujan, **jadi** saya di rumah*. Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata, jadinya 'Because it rained, so I stayed home', dan itu salah dalam bahasa Inggris.

rows.en: I was tired, so I went to bed early.
rows.id: Saya capek, jadi saya tidur lebih awal.

rows.en: I went to bed early because I was tired.
rows.id: Saya tidur lebih awal karena saya capek.

rows.en: Because I was tired, I went to bed early.
rows.id: Karena capek, saya tidur lebih awal.
rows.note: because first is fine too: no so

id.note: because di depan juga boleh: tanpa so

rows.en: The road was very busy, so Budi took an ojek.
rows.id: Jalannya macet sekali, jadi Budi naik ojek.

blocks.text: Another Indonesian trap: **akhirnya**. Often it means *jadi*: *Hujan deras, akhirnya kami tidak jadi pergi.* That's a **result**, so English uses **so**: *It rained hard, so we didn't go.* Use **finally** only for the last event or the end of a long wait. Also, you'll see **so** with another job: *It was **so** hot* = panas sekali (so = very). That's a different meaning.

id.text: Jebakan lain dari bahasa Indonesia: **akhirnya**. Sering artinya *jadi*: *Hujan deras, akhirnya kami tidak jadi pergi.* Itu **akibat**, jadi bahasa Inggrisnya pakai **so**: *It rained hard, so we didn't go.* Pakai **finally** hanya untuk kejadian terakhir atau akhir dari menunggu lama. Kamu juga akan melihat **so** dengan tugas lain: *It was **so** hot* = panas sekali (so = sangat). Itu arti yang berbeda.

blocks.prompt: Dimas had no money, ___ he went to the ATM.
blocks.explain: No money is the reason; going to the ATM is the result, so use **so**. because would make the ATM the reason, and finally is for the last event, not a result.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas had no money, ___ he went to the ATM.
id.explain: Tidak punya uang adalah alasannya; pergi ke ATM adalah akibatnya, jadi pakai **so**. because akan membuat ATM menjadi alasannya, dan finally untuk kejadian terakhir, bukan akibat.

id.title: so untuk akibat, because untuk alasan

blocks.text: Here is a short story with all the linking words from this lesson. Read it and find **First, Then, After that, Finally, before, after, when** and **so**. Look at the verbs too: they're all in the past simple, or *was / were*.

id.text: Ini cerita pendek dengan semua kata penghubung dari pelajaran ini. Bacalah dan temukan **First, Then, After that, Finally, before, after, when** dan **so**. Perhatikan juga kata kerjanya: semuanya past simple, atau *was / were*.

rows.en: Last Monday was a bad day for Sari.
rows.id: Senin lalu adalah hari yang buruk bagi Sari.

rows.en: First, she got up late, so she didn't have breakfast.
rows.id: Pertama-tama, dia bangun kesiangan, jadi dia tidak sarapan.

rows.en: Then she took an ojek to the office.
rows.id: Lalu dia naik ojek ke kantor.

rows.en: When she got there, Pak Hasan was angry.
rows.id: Ketika dia sampai di sana, Pak Hasan marah.

rows.en: After she said sorry, she started work.
rows.id: Setelah dia minta maaf, dia mulai bekerja.

rows.en: Before she went home, she bought a big martabak.
rows.id: Sebelum pulang, dia membeli martabak besar.

rows.en: Finally, she ate it with her family, so the day ended well.
rows.id: Akhirnya, dia memakannya bersama keluarganya, jadi harinya berakhir dengan baik.

blocks.text: When you tell your own story, start with **when** it happened (*Last Monday, Yesterday*), then use **First**, mix **then / next / after that** in the middle, and end with **Finally**. One linker per join is enough: **after** or **then**, **because** or **so**.

id.text: Saat kamu menceritakan ceritamu sendiri, mulai dengan **kapan** kejadiannya (*Last Monday, Yesterday*), lalu pakai **First**, campur **then / next / after that** di tengah, dan akhiri dengan **Finally**. Satu kata penghubung untuk tiap sambungan sudah cukup: **after** atau **then**, **because** atau **so**.

suggestedQuestions: What's the difference between then, next and after that?
Why can't I say 'Because it rained, so I stayed home'?
When do I put a comma with after and when?

id.intro: Sekarang kamu sudah bisa membicarakan masa lalu, jadi ayo bercerita! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan mengurutkan kejadian dengan **first, then, next, after that** dan **finally**, menggabungkannya dengan **before, after** dan **when**, dan menyatakan akibatnya dengan **so**. assessment.ls-1: Lengkapi ceritanya dengan First, Then dan Finally (pakai masing-masing satu kali). Tulis ketiga kata itu sesuai urutan: ___, I went to the ATM. ___ I bought some fruit at the market. ___, I went home and cooked dinner.
assessment.ls-2: Lengkapi dengan First atau Finally: We waited at the bus stop for an hour. ___, the bus came!
assessment.ls-3: Lengkapi dengan before atau after: Rina washed the vegetables ___ she cooked them.
assessment.ls-4: Perbaiki kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: After we had lunch, then we went back to the office.
assessment.ls-5: Gabungkan kedua kalimat dengan when: I got home. My mother was in the kitchen.
assessment.ls-6: Perbaiki kesalahannya dan tulis kalimat yang benar: Because the shop was closed, so we went to the warung.
assessment.ls-7: Gabungkan kedua kalimat dengan so: My phone was broken. I bought a new one.
